note: Research notes from outside the laboratory. Each says how it is known. None of these is a discovery: only experiments (knowledge.json) can make one. labStatus says what the laboratory has done with it.

grades.source: the code was cloned or fetched and read
grades.third-party: a write-up by someone else; not checked against the tool
grades.search-snippet: only a search-result summary was available
grades.unreachable: the host could not be reached from the research environment

sources.title: LuaXen (ByteXenon)
claims: MIT licence; a single commit, dated 2024-09-29 in the clone; 174 files.
A toolkit in pure Lua: lexer, parser, compiler, decompiler, minifier, interpreter, assembler, packer.
Its obfuscator example runs two stages in order: Obfuscator.IronBrikked.ObfuscateScript, then Obfuscator.ASTObfuscator.ObfuscateScript on the result: a nested, multi-stage case.
sources.labReason: Needs a real Lua runtime (package.path, debug.getinfo, require of its own modules). None is available in the research environment, so no sample output was produced and no compatibility claim exists.

sources.title: Luraph (lura.ph)
claims: The vendor site could not be reached from the research environment (the egress proxy refused the connection).

A web search found no official changelog. Third-party pages label obfuscated files v13.6.x, v14.3 and v14.4.1; none of them is a reliable source for how the versions differ, and no source found mentioned v15.
sources.labReason: No sample output of any Luraph version was available. The laboratory cannot generate Luraph output (commercial service). A person who owns Luraph output can add it as a supplied sample; until then nothing is claimed beyond what the detector's signatures already say.

sources.title: Prometheus documentation and issue tracker
claims: Upstream documentation has moved to prometheus-lua.github.io/Prometheus/docs; the GitBook copy labels itself a legacy mirror.
The issue tracker lists Vmify bugs, among them one where Vmify applied to the AntiTamper step's code can produce failing code (issue 155, reported Nov 2023).
sources.labReason: Prometheus is measured with real tool output in data/compat.json (docs/COMPATIBILITY.md), not by this laboratory.

sources.title: Hercules (zeusssz)
claims: Its README says the VirtualMachine and bytecode_encoding modules are disabled automatically for Luau output.
sources.labReason: Measured with real tool output in data/compat.json.

sources.title: Baza Obfuscator; EVIL AXE Studios
claims: Baza Obfuscator is advertised as a Discord bot with a ChaCha20-encrypted VM; its code is not published.
EVIL AXE Studios is described as a wrapper around Prometheus.
sources.labReason: No code and no sample output.

sources.title: ByteLuaObfuscator (kosuke14)
claims: A search listing describes a bytecode-method obfuscator without Luau support. A clone attempt was refused (the repository asked for credentials), so its code was not read.
